reasons: No tests are visible for this file.
Types are checked only at build time, so bad saved data is not caught.
Older deck formats are handled in other files, not checked here.

terms.meaning: A written description of what shape a piece of data must have, so a program can check it.
A field that may be left out. Code must handle its absence.
A pointer that says where a number or sentence came from, such as a project and a field name, or a web link.
A saved deck made before a newer field existed. It may lack that field.

sections.name: ScanElement
sections.title: One slide element
sections.what: Describes one item on a slide, such as a text box, rectangle, line, oval, or picture. It holds position and size on the 1280 by 720 canvas, the text and its styling, colours, the picture name if any, and where its facts came from.
sections.why: Likely reason: one element type lets the same slide be drawn on screen and exported to PowerPoint.
sections.watch_out: Font sizes are in points, but positions are in canvas units. Also, source and sources both exist for backward compatibility, so code must check both.

sections.name: ScanSourceRef, ScanBubbleSize, ScanChartView
sections.title: Citations and chart choices
sections.what: Defines the citation pointer, which names a project, a field, and optionally a quote, link, and formula with its inputs. It also defines the three bubble size options and the two chart views, delivery and portfolio.
sections.why: Likely reason: so every number on a slide can show where it came from, and the calculation can be traced.
sections.watch_out: Project citations and research citations use different required fields. Code that reads one kind must not assume the other kind has the same fields.

sections.name: ScanChartConfig
sections.title: Saved chart settings
sections.what: Stores the chosen bubble size and, optionally, the chart view, the selected project ids, and the filter choices.
sections.why: Likely reason: so a chart cut that a user set up can be reopened exactly as it was.
sections.watch_out: Only the bubble size is required. Older decks may have no saved settings at all, so the app must fall back to defaults.

sections.name: ScanSlide
sections.title: One slide
sections.what: Stores a slide's id, a layout name, its title, and its list of elements.
sections.why: Likely reason: a slide is the basic unit the editor and exporter draw.
sections.watch_out: The layout name is plain text, not a checked list, so a misspelled layout name is not caught by the types.

sections.name: ScanTemplateProject
sections.title: One project record
sections.what: Stores one project as frozen at the time of the run: name, country, industry, capacity, planned and actual budgets, cost and schedule percentages, dates, status, reasons, citations for each field, quality checks, and optional capacity, technology, and party names.
sections.why: Likely reason: values are frozen at run time so a deck always shows the same numbers, even if the source changes later.
sections.watch_out: Most numeric fields can be missing. Newer fields such as forecast and capacity values are absent in older decks, so code must not assume they exist.

sections.name: ScanTemplateInput
sections.title: Full input for a deck
sections.what: Holds everything needed to build a whole deck: title, industry, creation time, the project records, the findings for negative and positive columns, and the caveat text.
sections.why: Likely reason: one input object lets the deck be built from a single saved run.
sections.watch_out: The caveat is a required text field. Leaving it empty removes the standard warning from the deck.

sections.name: ScanProposal
sections.title: Suggested text change
sections.what: Describes a proposed wording change to one slide element. It records the old and new text, the reason, whether the change is editorial or factual, the deck revision it was based on, its status, and its supporting sources.
sections.why: Likely reason: proposals wait for a user decision, so they must be stored and tracked until applied or dismissed.
sections.watch_out: The basedOnRevision number shows whether the deck has changed since the proposal was made. Check it before applying a proposal, or the change may be out of date.

sections.name: ScanResearchSource
sections.title: Web research source
sections.what: Describes a web source found during research: its title, link, a short excerpt, whether the page could be fetched, and when it was checked.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the research evidence with the chat answers that used it.
sections.watch_out: The status shows how strong the evidence is. A search-only or unreachable source should not be presented as a verified page.

sections.name: ScanMessage
sections.title: One chat message
sections.what: Stores one message in the deck's assistant chat, tied to a slide, with optional research sources.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps each chat exchange linked to the slide it was about.
sections.watch_out: Only user and assistant are allowed as roles. Other message types must be added here first.

sections.name: ScanDeck
sections.title: The whole saved deck
sections.what: Stores the complete saved deck: its version, a revision counter, title, industry, dates, template name, slides, projects, caveat, chat messages, suggested changes, and the saved chart settings.
sections.why: Likely reason: one saved object holds everything the editor needs to reopen a deck.
sections.watch_out: The revision counter must rise with each change, because suggested changes compare against it. Version is fixed at 1, so a future format change needs a new version value.

summary: Defines the shapes of saved scan deck data: slides, elements, project records, citations, chat messages, suggested edits, research sources, and the whole deck.
purpose: Gives every other file one agreed description of what a deck contains, so data saved by one part of the app is read the same way by the others.
why: Likely reason: the editor, the exporter, and the saved files all need the same layout. Comments show where older saved decks need fallbacks.
how: The file is only type definitions. It has no running logic. Each definition names the fields, their types, and which fields are optional. Other files use these definitions to check their data during development.
inputs: None at run time. Other files read these definitions.
outputs: None at run time. The definitions exist only for the development-time type checker.
risks: Types are checked when the code is built, not when real saved data is loaded. An old or hand-edited deck can therefore break the app without a clear error. Many fields are optional, so code that reads them must handle missing values.
debug: If a field looks missing or wrong, compare it with the saved deck file and check whether the field is optional. If the build reports type errors after a change here, other files that use the same type are affected.
